chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive to cause corruption in the land is that they be killed or crucified or that their hands and feet be cut off,' up to the end of the verse.
So I said, 'Which of these penalties, which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has named, is upon them?'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is for the Imam; if he wills, he cuts (the hand), and if he wills, he crucifies, and if he wills, he exiles, and if he wills, he kills.'
I said, 'Exile to where?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'He is exiled from one city to another city.'
And he (peace be upon him) said, 'Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) exiled two men from Kufa to Basra.'

key_terms.مِنْ مِصْرٍ إِلَى مِصْرٍ: from one city to another city

ai.seo_question: What are the four punishments for muharibin and who decides which one to apply?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Imam’s judicial discretion (iktisar) in applying the hudud for al-muharibin, confirming that the four Quranic penalties are not cumulative but alternative options chosen by the Imam based on context. It further clarifies the practical definition of exile (nafi) as relocation between cities, supported by the historical precedent of Imam Ali banishing individuals from Kufa to Basra. This establishes the Imam’s authority to tailor the punishment to the specific nature of the corruption, reflecting the flexibility inherent in Shia jurisprudence regarding capital and corporal crimes.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [5:33] But rather, the Recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Rasool and strive to make mischief in the land is only this, that they should be killed or crucified or their hands and their feet should be cut off – up to the end of the Verse’.
So I said, ‘Which thing is upon them from these Penalties which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Mentioned?’

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That is upon the Imam<sup>asws</sup>, if he<sup>asws</sup> so desires to, he<sup>asws</sup> cuts, and if he<sup>asws</sup> so desires to he<sup>asws</sup> crucifies, and if he<sup>asws</sup> so desires to he<sup>asws</sup> exiles, and if he<sup>asws</sup> so desires to he<sup>asws</sup> kills’.
I said, ‘The exiling is to where?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be exiled from a city to another city’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> exiled two men from Al-Kufa to Al-Basra’.
